Zscaler, which had a market value of $32 billion at the end of regular trading Friday, rose about 16% after the close. Bloomberg News Deals Reporter Ryan Gould reports on the deal. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 21 日消息，有零跑 A10 车主用户近日发布视频，反馈自己车辆的后备箱在装了几箱啤酒后被压穿底。随后，该事件引发网友热议。IT之家注意到，针对网传情况，零跑汽车官方在昨晚 23:05 发布情况说明：关于零跑 A10 后备厢储物盒的情况说明近日，我们关注到网络上流传的零跑 A10 后备厢下层储物盒受损的相关视频。公司高度重视，第一时间联系用户并对车辆进行了检测。经核实，本次受损部件为后备厢盖板下方的独立储物盒，系装载物品超过其设计承重上限所致，并非后备厢底板或整车承载结构受损。我们已与用户充分沟通并获得了用户的理解。零跑 A10 采用双层后备厢布局：上层为主载物空间，满足日常大件及重物装载需求；盖板下方配备下沉式储物盒，定位干湿分离与轻量收纳。根据《用户手册》，该储物盒最大承重为 40kg。车辆日常装载重物、大件及高密度物品时，建议放置于上层主载物区。这次事件也反映出我们在用车指引和场景化提示上仍有不足，后续我们将在新车交付、车机界面及官方平台发布的用车指引中进行优化。感谢媒体朋友、广大车主及社会各界的关注与监督，我们将持续为用户提供可靠的产品与贴心的服务。零跑汽车2026 年 11 月 20 日官方示意图如下：

articles.title: AI 攻克黎曼猜想？Anthropic 数学家宣称已与 Claude 合作完成证明
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据《科学美国人》报道，当地时间 20 日，Anthropic 数学家莱文特 · 阿尔波格宣称，自己与 AI 模型 Claude 合作，攻克了数学界最著名的难题之一 —— 黎曼猜想。阿尔波格在个人网站发表声明称：“我相信，我与 Claude 合作找到了黎曼猜想的证明。”IT之家注：黎曼猜想由德国数学家伯恩哈德 · 黎曼于 1859 年提出，认为看似随机分布在数轴上的质数，实际上遵循着复杂而有意义的规律。此后，黎曼猜想成为整个数论研究领域的重要指引，也是数学界最著名的未解难题。由于长期缺乏明确的证明思路，研究进展极其有限，就连顶尖数学家也很少花费大量时间直接尝试证明。直到今年 10 月，OpenAI 集中公布的一批数学研究成果中，有一项证明在揭示质数分布规律方面取得重大进展，让攻克黎曼猜想首次看到了突破口。漫长的求证之路似乎即将走到终点。阿尔波格公布了与 Claude 合作完成的证明，并将其编写为 Lean 代码。据悉，Lean 是一种能够逐步验证数学推理是否正确的编程语言。一旦得到确认，2026 年将成为 AI 数学能力实现飞跃的一年。报道说，AI 从此前表现不稳定、甚至难以达到大学生水平，发展到展现出超越人类的能力，数学领域的各个分支都将受到冲击。阿尔波格称，他的证明不仅解决了黎曼猜想，还证明了范围远比原始猜想广泛的“广义黎曼猜想”。广义黎曼猜想，则意味着整个数学世界蕴藏着无数尚未发现的深层规律。如果这一成果得到确认，对数学界的影响将难以估量，大量以广义黎曼猜想成立为前提的数学结论也将随之得到证实。阿尔波格的声明既流露出对一个时代结束的伤感，也表达了对未来的期待。“觉得这一切意味着某种终结，是很自然的。对我而言，这意味着失去了一盏重要的指路明灯。但研究过程中见证的进展令我如此震撼，让我相信，整个科学界正在迎来远比其更伟大事物的曙光。”阿尔波格最后写道：“我希望这一证明能让人们一窥未来的奇迹，也让我们感受到，即使是最简单的事物，也将带给我们怎样的喜悦与惊奇。”参考论文原文（https://alpo.ge/remark.pdf）

articles.title: 在欧洲已拿下 12 国，特斯拉辅助驾驶系统获意大利运行许可
articles.content: 特斯拉辅助驾驶系统（TAD）获得意大利运行许可，成为继此前 11 个欧盟国家之后，又一个获准使用该系统的市场。当地时间 11 月 20 日，意大利交通部向特斯拉辅助驾驶系统颁发临时型式认证。交通部长马泰奥 · 萨尔维尼在 X 上宣布这一消息，称此举是朝着创新、科技和未来出行迈出的又一步，同时始终将公共安全放在首位。意大利交通部在全面评估技术可行性后作出批准决定。意大利由此成为欧洲第 12 个放行该系统的国家，也是欧盟主要汽车市场中首个批准该系统的国家。特斯拉辅助驾驶系统此前名为 FSD（监督版），近期将在意大利通过 OTA 升级推送，订阅价格为每月 99 欧元。意大利的批准比此前其他国家的放行更具分量。今年 4 月，特斯拉辅助驾驶系统首次获得荷兰车辆管理局的临时型式认证，随后又陆续获得立陶宛、丹麦、比利时、克罗地亚和芬兰等国批准，但这些国家大多规模较小。意大利则不同。作为欧盟人口第三大国，意大利与德国、法国和西班牙同属欧盟传统四大主要国家。意大利城市道路密集、交通环境复杂，对辅助驾驶系统的实际表现考验也比此前许多获批市场更加严苛。此次批准之前，马斯克曾在 10 月下旬与萨尔维尼交谈，后者随后公开支持欧盟尽快批准该系统在整个欧盟范围内使用。按照欧盟的特定多数表决规则，统一批准需要至少 15 个成员国支持，且支持国家的人口合计须占欧盟总人口的 65% 以上。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据《财富》杂志今日报道，过去一周，美国接连发生多起技术故障，导致航班停飞、银行交易延误，数百万人无法正常使用电子邮件，暴露出美国基础设施的脆弱性。美国电网同样存在短板，问题出在铜和钢等材料的供应上。约翰斯 · 霍普金斯大学近日在《Cell Reports Sustainability》期刊发表的一项研究显示，美国最早可能在 2027 年就面临电网设备短缺，影响新建电厂和数据中心并网。到 2030 年，变压器和变流器的短缺问题或将进一步恶化。对于企业和普通家庭来说，最直接的影响将是电费上涨、停电更加频繁。参与研究的约翰斯 · 霍普金斯大学副教授尤里 · 德沃尔金与博士生 Boyu Yao 分析了电网设备供应问题。“过去，人们从不担心这些设备的供应。但缺少它们，即使建好了数据中心或发电厂，也无法接入电网，自然就无法供电。当电力需求增长速度超过预期时，行业原有的种种问题就更加突出了。”美国电力行业面临的压力还在迅速增加。研究显示，美国用电量过去每年通常增长 1% 至 2%，随着 AI 数据中心、电动汽车和各行业电气化进程推高电力需求，预计到 2030 年将增长 21%。这其中，数据中心预计占到预期设备缺口的三分之二。美国电气制造商协会还预计，到 2050 年，美国电力需求增幅将超过 50%。现有电网难以承受如此快速的需求增长。哥伦比亚商学院数据显示，美国超过 70% 的输电线路使用年限超过 20 年，而电力公司要满足 AI 企业眼下的用电需求，还需要数年时间建设新的供电设施并完成并网。制造变压器和其他电网设备需要铜、钢、镍、铝和锰。研究发现，未来四年，美国恐将面临这五种材料的全面短缺。最先出现供应缺口的预计是铜，时间最早就在 2027 年。影响范围不仅限于电网，还会波及数据中心设备、风电变流器和纯电汽车充电设施。随后是钢和镍，研究预计，到 2030 年，这两种材料将变得极难采购。如果电力需求持续高涨，未来四年美国变压器供应缺口将接近 15%，其他关键电网设备的缺口则达到 30%。如果再发生贸易中断，导致来自不稳定贸易伙伴的原材料供应最多下降 70%，变压器缺口将扩大至约 25%，其他关键设备的缺口也会升至 36%。即使用电需求增长相对温和，其他电网配套设备仍将面临约 16% 的供应缺口，但变压器供应能够满足需求。美国能源部今年 9 月承诺向 31 个项目投入 19 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 127.15 亿元人民币），以提高现有输电线路的输电能力并降低成本。但与电网实际需要的资金相比，这笔投资远远不够。摩根大通估计，到 2035 年，美国电网需要投入约 1 万亿美元（现汇率约合 6.69 万亿元人民币）。投资不仅要用于扩建电网，还要更换老旧设备。美国大量电网设施接近使用寿命终点，老旧变压器需要翻新或更换，与新建项目争夺本就紧张的设备供应。不断上涨的维护费用也开始推高美国居民的电费账单。制造商同样难以跟上需求。变压器通常采用定制生产，过去四年交货周期延长至原来的四倍，从约六个月增加到两年多。大型电力变压器还需要使用取向电工钢，而美国只有一家钢厂能够生产这种材料。研究人员提出了几种缓解短缺的办法：安装低成本传感器，实时监测变压器负载；回收退役设备中的材料；以及推动变压器设计标准化，让不同设备能够相互替换，从而提高现有资源的利用效率。

articles.title: 伦敦交通局遭网络攻击，26.5 万名“牡蛎”交通卡用户数据泄露
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据外媒 Neowin 今天（20 日）晚间报道，伦敦交通局（TfL）证实，黑客入侵导致 26.5 万名 Oyster（牡蛎）照片卡用户的敏感信息泄露。▲ 图源英国政府网站Oyster 照片卡是伦敦公共交通系统使用的一种实名交通卡，符合条件的老年居民、退伍军人、儿童、学生、学徒和结束社会照护的青年，可以凭卡免费或优惠乘车。与可以匿名使用的普通 Oyster 卡不同，Oyster 照片卡记录了持卡人的姓名、住址、出生日期及照片等个人信息。伦敦交通局确认，持有 Zip Oyster 卡的儿童姓名和出生日期没有泄露。用户密码、银行账户及支付卡信息、乘车记录和照片卡上的照片也未受影响。可能受影响的账户涉及以下卡种：Zip Oyster 卡（5—10 岁、11—15 岁、16 岁及以上）18 岁及以上学生 Oyster 卡18—25 岁结束社会照护青年 Oyster 照片卡60 岁及以上伦敦居民 Oyster 照片卡退伍军人 Oyster 照片卡学徒 Oyster 照片卡伦敦交通局发现，部分原本拥有账户的用户收到官方邮件被要求重新注册账户，由此察觉系统遭到入侵。这些邮件是在系统被攻破后产生的，表明黑客可能直接利用伦敦交通局的官方系统发送欺诈邮件，而不是伪造发件人身份。随后，伦敦交通局关闭了 Oyster 照片卡网站。伦敦交通局技术战略与营收总监沙希 · 维尔玛确认，安全事件已得到控制。“由于我们及时发现并处理了此次事件，相信可能受到影响的用户数量大幅减少。我们仍在调查事件的具体经过，但已联系受影响的用户，告知他们有关情况。”伦敦交通局还向英国信息专员办公室（ICO）通报了此次事件。IT之家获悉，该机构是英国负责监管数据隐私和信息权利的独立机构。伦敦交通局要求所有 Oyster 照片卡用户修改账户密码、安全问题及答案。如果其他网站或网络服务使用了相同密码，也必须更换，以防黑客进一步入侵其他账户。

articles.title: 内存成本涨幅前所未有，Valve 坦承 Steam Machine 未来售价“无法得知”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，AI 热潮引发的内存危机波及几乎所有消费电子产品，Steam Machine 也未能幸免。由于需求旺盛，Valve 直到近期才完成 512GB 版的全部预订订单。目前该版本尚有少量现货，消费者可以直接下单，无需继续排队。好消息之外还有坏消息。Valve 透露，Steam Machine 仍在持续生产，但内存和存储设备的成本正以前所未有的幅度上涨。受此影响，后续还能生产多少台、售价会是多少，都无法给出明确答案，价格也有进一步上涨的可能，更多消息预计将在 2027 年 1 月公布。Steam Machine 上市时，512GB 版和 2TB 版分别定价 1,049 美元（现汇率约合 7,020 元人民币）和 1,349 美元（现汇率约合 9,027 元人民币），均不附赠手柄。两款机型相差 300 美元（现汇率约合 2,008 元人民币），区别仅在于存储容量，处理器、显卡和内存配置完全相同，均采用 Zen 4 架构六核处理器、配备 8GB 显存的 RDNA 3 架构显卡，以及 16GB 内存。Steam Machine 的上市价格依据此前六个月的零部件采购成本制定。Valve 曾表示，这款主机基本按成本价出售，几乎没有余地承担内存和 SSD 继续涨价的成本。今年 6 月，Valve 还以 Steam Deck OLED 为例说明存储成本上涨的影响：512GB 版和 1TB 版分别涨价 240 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,606 元人民币）和 300 美元，大致可以据此判断 Steam Machine 的售价比最初计划高出了多少。2TB 版的供货情况更加严峻。Valve 已向所有获得预订资格的消费者发送购买邀请，没有抢到预订资格的人就只能进入另一份候补名单，而排队人数甚至超过了现有供货量。即使后续能够买到更多零部件，Valve 预计 2TB 版的产量仍会低于原计划。目前，Valve 已关闭 2TB 版的候补申请通道。排队中的消费者可以保留原有位置，但不保证最终能够买到机器。用户也可以选择购买仍有现货的 512GB 版，不过必须放弃 2TB 版的候补资格。512GB 版的现有库存卖完后更是直接显示缺货，Valve 也不会再开放新的候补名单。

articles.title: 德国首家，奔驰获批在“老家”开展点到点辅助驾驶
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，梅赛德斯-奔驰今天（20 日）宣布，成为德国首家获得点到点辅助驾驶监管许可的车企，为高级自动驾驶技术在公共道路上的应用取得重要突破。这是德国首次依据联合国高级驾驶辅助系统新规颁发此类许可。各大车企也在竞相拓展自动驾驶功能的使用场景，突破以往主要局限于高速公路的限制。此次获批的 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO 系统，可将驾驶辅助功能从高速公路延伸至城市道路，驾驶员仍须掌握车辆控制权。奔驰计划今年年底在斯图加特和慕尼黑启动先期体验计划，2027 年上半年再逐步推广至德国其他地区。据IT之家了解，随着联合国新规于 2027 年 1 月生效，未来还可将该系统引入其他采用相同法规的国家。奔驰此前推出的 DRIVE PILOT 系统允许驾驶员在特定条件下不必持续注视路面。新获批的 MB.DRIVE ASSIST PRO 系统自动驾驶程度则较低，却能适应城市交通场景等更多道路环境。

articles.title: Anthropic 上市次日股价下跌 9%，AI 板块雪上加霜
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据路透社报道，当地时间 20 日，Anthropic 上市次日股价下跌，令低迷的 AI 板块雪上加霜。这场备受期待的 IPO，也没能重新点燃投资者的热情。作为 AI 投资热潮的重要风向标，Anthropic 上市曾被寄予厚望，市场期待借此提振经历一段动荡时期后持续疲软的 AI 板块。然而，Anthropic 股价报 88.25 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 590.6 元人民币），较上市首日的收盘价下跌约 9%。公司完全稀释后的估值约为 1.6 万亿美元（现汇率约合 10.71 万亿元人民币），按已发行股份计算的市值则约为 1.2 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.03 万亿元人民币）。短期内，股价仍可能持续波动。随着上市热潮逐渐退去，投资者开始审视 Anthropic 相当于过去 12 个月营收约 40 倍的估值是否合理。美国合众银行资产管理部门私人市场投资主管考希 · 阿明建议：“我们倾向于对 Anthropic 保持耐心，等公司陆续公布上市后的业绩，再进行评估。”在他看来，当前估值意味着，市场预期 Anthropic 未来多年都能保持快速增长。Anthropic 上市也未能扭转市场对 AI 板块的担忧。华尔街主要股指周四大幅收跌，周五的股指期货走势则预示市场可能继续下挫。美股科技七巨头中，英伟达和 Meta 盘前跌幅均超过 3%，亚马逊和微软跌幅超过 2%。芯片股同样承压，AMD 和闪迪均下跌超过 6%，英特尔跌幅超过 4%。市场接下来的关注焦点是 OpenAI 可能进行的 IPO。OpenAI 此前透露有望于明年上市，届时将再次检验投资者对 AI 股票的兴趣。散户 19 日当天买卖 Anthropic 股票的交易额约为 7.72 亿美元（现汇率约合 51.66 亿元人民币），创下研究机构 Vanda Research 自 2012 年开始统计以来，IPO 首日散户交易额的最高纪录。Anthropic 股价大幅波动，让投资者面临两难选择：究竟应该押注股价反弹，还是防范进一步下跌？Anthropic 股票期权预计下周开始交易，可能进一步加剧波动。德国贝伦贝格银行指数事件主管卡斯滕 · 黑塞指出，目前的市场环境对 Anthropic 并不有利。竞争加剧也可能削弱投资者的信心。彭博社最新消息称，苹果正在开发一款能够代替用户执行任务的 AI 智能体，准备加入 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Meta 之间的市场竞争。

articles.title: 比亚迪腾势汽车李慧：易三方 Evo 是全球独一无二的硬核技术平台，友商追赶了易三方超过三年也没追上
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，博主 @向北不断电 今日发文，称腾势 N8 的优势依然明显，也是市面上为数不多闭眼买的车型，并提到易三方 Evo 独一档强大。腾势汽车总经理李慧随后转发，并表示易三方 Evo 是全球独一无二的硬核技术平台，目前任何一个汽车品牌都没有，友商追赶了易三方超过三年也没有追赶上。易三方 Evo 让腾势 N8 更安全、更灵活、更澎湃、更高效！据IT之家此前报道，腾势 N8 于 11 月 12 日正式上市，共推出 6 款配置车型，提供后置单电机两驱与易三方三电机四驱两种动力形式，官方指导价区间为 26.99 万-32.99 万元。延伸阅读易三方（e³）是比亚迪旗下腾势品牌独有的整车智能控制技术平台，于 2024 年 9 月随腾势 Z9GT 首次量产搭载。该平台由三电机独立驱动技术、后轮双电机独立转向技术、VMC 整车运动控制技术、CTB 电池车身一体化技术四大核心技术组成，可实现后轮双向最大 20° 的独立转向，并衍生出极致转向、圆规掉头、易三方泊车、低附路面增稳系统、智能蟹行等功能。此次腾势 N8 全球首搭的「易三方 Evo」是该平台的升级版本。据官方介绍，其在效率上有所提升，可使整车续航提升超过 60km，并进一步强化安全能力，通过了高速直线侧后追尾稳行、湿滑路面高速连续避障、夜间及弯道湿滑路面侧后追尾稳行等四大工况测试，同时全系标配第二代刀片电池与 CTB 电池车身一体化技术。腾势 N8 定位「科技新境宽五座 SUV」，于 2026 年 11 月 12 日上市，提供纯电与插混两种动力。该车车身尺寸为 5150×1999×1820mm，轴距 3075mm，最小转弯半径 4.5m，后轮转向角度为 ±10°，0-100km/h 加速时间为 4.3 秒。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据韩联社当地时间 18 日报道，根据三星电子同日发布的详细三季报，该企业负责非半导体板块的 DX（设备体验）部门今年 1~9 月的内存平均采购价格同比暴涨 263%。而在相同时间内，DX 部门的移动应用处理器平均采购价格上涨了 8%，旗下 MX（移动体验）业务的 Galaxy 智能手机平均销售价格仅上涨了 13%。另一组数据显示，DX 部门 1~9 月原材料采购额达 62.4307 万亿韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,132.77 亿元人民币），同比增长 8.9%；移动设备内存采购总额达 7.6993 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 386.35 亿元人民币），占整体的 12.3%。内存成本暴涨但终端设备售价涨幅有限，导致 MX 与 NW（网络）业务整体连续第二个季度出现亏损。MX 业务在 Q3 财报电话会议中表示，计划以差异化的旗舰产品为核心，以硬件和形态创新增强用户吸引力，并通过灵活市场响应和运营改进降低利润下滑影响。

articles.title: 我国成功发射卫星互联网低轨 30 组卫星
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，今天（20 日）19 时 59 分，我国在海南商业航天发射场使用长征八号甲运载火箭，成功将卫星互联网低轨 30 组卫星发射升空，卫星顺利进入预定轨道，发射任务获得圆满成功。据IT之家了解，11 月 9 日 4 时 24 分，长征十二号运载火箭在海南商业航天发射场点火起飞，随后成功将卫星互联网低轨 29 组卫星送入预定轨道。延伸阅读卫星互联网低轨卫星组网属于中国星网 GW 星座，这是我国首个巨型卫星互联网计划，也是我国首个空天一体化 6G 卫星互联网计划。整个星座规划部署 12992 颗卫星，分为 GW-A59 与 GW-A2 两个子星座：前者计划部署 6080 颗，主要分布在 500 公里以下轨道；后者计划部署 6912 颗，轨道高度约 1145 公里，轨道倾角覆盖 30 度至 85 度。按照相关规划，GW 星座将在 2029 年年底前完成约 1300 颗卫星部署，并计划于 2035 年完成全部 12992 颗卫星组网。2026 年 10 月 9 日，国产卫星系统在中国第 16 次北冰洋考察期间完成首次极区试验，实现跨越南北极的视频通话，测试使用的正是中国星网 GW 星座，最高上下行速率约 30Mbps。而本次使用的长征八号甲运载火箭由航天科技集团一院研制，是长征八号运载火箭的改进型号，采用 3.35 米直径氢氧末级和 5.2 米直径整流罩，全箭高超 50 米，起飞质量约 371 吨，起飞推力约 480 吨，700 公里太阳同步轨道运载能力提升至 7 吨级，专为高密度、快速组网发射而设计。

articles.title: 加州禁令引发连锁反应，Waymo 暂停全美 Robotaxi 高速公路服务
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，当地时间 18 日，据英国《卫报》报道，Alphabet 旗下的 Waymo 在美国全面暂停了无人驾驶出租车的高速公路服务，恢复时间未定。此前，加州因 Waymo 车辆近期发生的交通事件，禁止其在州内高速公路行驶，Waymo 随后将暂停范围扩大至全美。Waymo 此前在旧金山湾区、洛杉矶、凤凰城、迈阿密和奥斯汀提供高速公路无人驾驶出租车服务，并在拉斯维加斯、达拉斯和丹佛等多个地区运营城市道路乘车服务，面向城区的服务此次不受影响。Waymo 发言人通过电子邮件回应称，公司暂时停止了所有运营市场的商业无人驾驶高速公路服务，但仍会让经过培训的自动驾驶专员坐在驾驶位，继续开展高速公路测试。暂停措施从 11 月 11 日开始实施，发言人没有透露恢复时间。同一天，加州机动车管理局也禁止 Waymo 无人驾驶出租车在州内高速公路行驶。该局发言人乔纳森 · 格罗夫曼指出，禁令与两起交通事件有关，其中一起是 3 辆 Waymo 无人驾驶车辆闯入施工区域。其中，施工区域事件发生在 11 月 5 日，另一起事件发生在 6 日，涉及加州公路巡警车辆，地点位于旧金山的一条高速公路。11 月 6 日事件的视频上周在社交媒体上广泛传播。画面显示，一辆 Waymo 试图绕过正在实施临时交通管制的加州公路巡警车辆。格罗夫曼指出，Waymo 车辆多次闯入仍在施工的区域，现场有施工人员、车辆和设备。加州机动车管理局因此认定，Waymo 的无人驾驶高速公路运营对公共安全构成直接威胁。而在 5 月 18 日，就已经发生了类似事件。Waymo 发言人则称，近期车辆在加州 101 号公路施工区域发生的事件没有造成人员受伤或车辆碰撞。格罗夫曼指出，加州禁令不仅禁止 Waymo 在高速公路运营无人驾驶车辆，也禁止开展无人驾驶测试。只有 Waymo 向监管部门证明采取了有效整改措施，解决引发禁令的问题后，限制措施才会解除。相关阅读：《美国加州叫停 Waymo 高速公路运营：无人驾驶出租车曾试图超越公路巡警》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，据 IGN 今天（20 日）晚间报道，《堡垒之夜》新增了一系列致敬《GTA 4》的隐藏任务，连游戏中的主要角色 Roman Bellic 那句经典的“表弟！咱们出去玩吧！”也被做成了彩蛋。11 月 19 日《GTA 6》正式发售当天，Epic Games 在《堡垒之夜》中开放了 6 项隐藏任务。玩家需要完成香蕉人皮利布置的任务，全部完成后可获得总计 12 万经验值。这些任务都在致敬《GTA 4》中 Roman 频繁打电话骚扰表弟、游戏主角 Niko 的经典桥段。玩家会在《堡垒之夜》中接到 Peely 的电话，随后按照要求完成附近的任务。其中一项任务要求玩家击倒保龄球瓶，呼应 Roman 经常打电话约 Niko 打保龄球的情节。任务说明更是直接写着：“表弟！咱们出去玩吧！”其他任务则围绕《堡垒之夜》现有地图上的彩蛋展开，包括探索隐藏的藏宝洞穴、破解类似《塞尔达传说》的雕像谜题，以及参加一场有趣的橡皮鸭竞赛。面对本周发售的《GTA 6》，《堡垒之夜》的表现依然相当稳健，常驻大逃杀模式的玩家数量仍达到数百万。据IT之家了解，Epic Games 还通过当前赛季的奖励活动吸引玩家，提供解锁为期两周免费使用游戏道具商店权限的机会，大批玩家正努力完成任务以获取这项福利。《GTA 6》方面，R 星尚未公布具体销量。不过，据估计，游戏发售前的预购量就达到 2000 万份，取得巨大成功自是不言而喻。

articles.title: Take-Two 前 CEO 费德：《GTA 6》将是 AI 时代前夜最后的“传统”3A 大作
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 20 日消息，Take-Two 前 CEO 本 · 费德认为，《GTA 6》将成为 AI 时代全面到来前最后一部采用传统开发模式打造的 3A 大作，游戏行业也将由此告别一个时代。费德在《财富》杂志撰文称：“《GTA 6》的发布将成为一场文化盛事，带来史诗般的游戏体验。我相信它会是一部杰作，但也会是同类作品中的最后一部。”IT之家获悉，他认为，原因并非 R 星的质量把控能力下降，也不是 AI 能让游戏开发更快、更省钱，而是《GTA 6》代表着一种即将被 AI 颠覆的创作模式的巅峰。费德指出，游戏开发过程中，改变方向甚至放弃原有创意，都可能耗费大量时间和技术资源，AI 可以大幅降低改变主意的成本。费德将 AI 对游戏行业的影响，比作摄影术对绘画的冲击：“摄影术问世时，许多视觉艺术家担心生计受到威胁，其中一些人的担忧确实成真了：委托画家绘制肖像的市场崩溃了。但也有人开始思考另一个问题：接下来我们还能创作什么？摆脱了忠实还原现实的要求后，他们开创了全新甚至颠覆性的艺术形式，包括印象派、立体主义和抽象艺术。我猜想，未来的文化史学家看待《GTA 6》，就像艺术史学家看待最后一批伟大的写实主义画家一样。”在他看来，《GTA 6》是一种创作模式在媒介边界被打破、全新艺术形式涌现之前所达到的最高成就。

articles.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are insatiable, the alignment required approaches perfect alignment as AI capability grows. Thus, mutualism is not a substitute for alignment. And when AI variants that keep more resources spread faster, al

articles.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We implement this by adding a separate, third-person observer role that answers these queries, which we can train solely for accuracy and separately from the assistant. articles.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. articles.content:

Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever.
  To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse compute architectures. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout generation, representation translation, response prediction, simulator-based validation, design diagnosis and improvement, structural understanding, and response classification. articles.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23445v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage pointwise projections and depthwise layers. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23454v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based clinical note generation. Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. Using annotated reference items, the framework anchors generation to the requested examination section and cognitive reasoning level, then applies sequential automated verification and guided repair before submitting drafts for expert review. articles.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories against these checks, pinning mastered rules while prioritizing newly broken behaviors, and selects among parallel candidate edits by critic-free group-relative fitness. articles.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question ends if the answer is unchanged and confident. articles.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every other token retains standard causal attention. articles.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answers and requiring no additional task executions. articles.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. BeFit (i) finds compact Bernstein-activated convolutional neural networks (BeCNNs) through hardware-aware neural architecture search and trains them via knowledge distillation; (ii) projects their weights to multiplication-free codes, freezes the codes, and recovers the resulting accuracy loss through the learnable activations; and (iii) generates model-specific kernels that exploit the projected weights for multiplication-free convolutions. articles.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23560v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. It remains open whether a more deliberate combination of the two views, and a decomposition of the prediction target, can recover more of the signal. We present a three-phase framework for estimating Big Five personality domain scores from life-narrative interview text. It encodes text and psycholinguistic features separately and combines them by concatenation or by a learned weighting, decomposes each domain into contrastively trained facet embeddings instead of predicting the domain directly, and pools the facet embeddings by attention into a domain-level prediction. articles.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods across multiple-choice, yes/no, open-ended question answering, and mathematical reasoning tasks. Abstract: Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. Such guidance must connect eligibility requirements, practical access constraints, and dietary needs rather than return isolated listings or generic nutritional advice. Multi-agent food assistants can coordinate these tasks, with uncertainty indicating when clarification or verification is needed before a recommendation. However, uncertainty can be lost across agent handoffs, allowing tentative interpretations to propagate as facts and obscuring opportunities for correction. articles.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, ARISE-Teacher, which uses Claude Opus 4.6 for attribution and consolidation, gains 10.9 pp over the baseline on SOP-Bench and 5.8 pp on $\tau^2$-bench. articles.content:

Abstract: Understanding how stable psychometric traits and time-varying states jointly inform behavior is an important problem in computational behavioral science. Existing personalized agents commonly condition actions directly on a static profile, leaving realized state transitions unused as an explicit source of supervision. We introduce a profile-conditioned state world model that uses observed environment--behavior state transitions to learn transition-informed representations for behavioral prediction. During training, a posterior encoder quantizes realized transitions, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25000v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned models by adding their task vectors to a shared backbone. Interference is typically assessed only after constructing and evaluating a candidate merge, making coefficient search expensive. We show that a first-order directional derivative of task A's outputs along task B's vector can predict interference, but only when evaluated at the appropriate model.
  At the receiver model, this derivative forecasts nearby merges per task and per example, halves the accuracy error of a no-change baseline, and identifies most examples whose predictions flip. For full multi-task merges, a single evaluation is insufficient; two evaluations along the merge path are needed. At the shared pretrained backbone, however, the derivative is nearly orthogonal to realized changes in our vision experiments and only partly predictive in LoRA language-model pilots. articles.title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25001v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generator-based sparse adversarial attacks train encoder--decoder networks to produce transferable sparse perturbations for black-box robustness evaluation. Their perturbation density, however, is set only indirectly by a fixed sparsity coefficient whose mapping to density is unknown and shifts during training, so reaching a target density requires re-tuning; this fixed pressure also yields little transferability gain once density reduction begins. We propose Density Feedback Control (DFC), which tightens or relaxes this coefficient at the end of each epoch according to the gap between the observed hard-mask density and the target, without changing the generator architecture or loss. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. arXiv:2611.25004v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adversarial attacks have posed significant threats to machine learning models by exploiting their inherent vulnerabilities. Researchers have established an interdisciplinary field called adversarial machine learning to explore these vulnerabilities and develop corresponding defense strategies. Feature reduction strategies are used to decrease the dimensionality of the data in order to reduce training time, avoid the curse of dimensionality, prevent overfitting, and mitigate redundant features. However, their effect on adversarial robustness across different classifiers and attack scenarios remains insufficiently explored. This study aims to analyze the effect of feature reduction techniques on the adversarial robustness of a diverse set of machine learning models under poisoning, backdoor, and universal adversarial perturbation attacks on the APT dataset. articles.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
  The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending only on $d$, due to Moran and Yehudayoff (2016), is exponential in $d$. We prove the weaker conjecture by constructing a sample compression scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$.

Abstract: Bayesian Optimization (BO) can be substantially more sample-efficient when informed by prior knowledge about the problem. In practice, however, such knowledge is often available only in natural language, e.g., expert intuitions or documentation, rather than as the explicit probability distribution landscape that prior-guided BO methods may require. Abstract: Face presentation attack detection (PAD) systems deployed in border control and airport surveillance are constrained by a critical assumption: subjects are captured at close range, typically under one meter. No existing benchmark systematically addresses multi-distance capture, diverse environmental conditions, and concurrent spoofing and occlusion-based attacks, leaving deployed models underprepared for real-world scenarios. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DISCO is a recent internal cluster validity index for density-based clustering that, unlike earlier indices, also evaluates the quality of noise labels. The discoCVI package makes DISCO available in R. This article describes the design of the package and a typical workflow, in which DISCO is used to compare clusterings and to choose the parameters of HDBSCAN without ground truth, followed by the implementation introduced in version 0.2.0. DISCO is defined through density-connectivity distances between all pairs of points, so direct implementations store several n-by-n matrices. We show that every quantity DISCO needs can be read off the single-linkage merge tree of the mutual-reachability minimum spanning tree, so that the index can be computed exactly with memory that grows linearly with the number of points, while the running time remains quadratic as in the original definition. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study active exploration for minimax transition estimation in unknown Markov decision processes (MDPs). Frequentist $\kappa$-Explorer~\citep{gu2026kappa} addresses this problem through a parameterized family of exploration objectives, but requires confidence-bound constructions and joint optimization over plausible transition kernels and occupancy measures, introducing a computational burden that limits its practical applicability. We develop Bayesian $\kappa$-Explorer, which simplifies this procedure by placing Dirichlet priors on the transition distributions. Under the posterior mean estimator, the posterior expected squared $\ell_2$ error equals the total posterior variance, providing a closed-form exploration signal. The algorithm plans under the posterior mean model, eliminating confidence-set optimization. articles.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25185v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. articles.title: {\phi}TD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.

Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. Abstract: Converting complex documents into structured knowledge constitutes the critical infrastructure urgently required for deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in downstream research. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These results demonstrate that multi-hop global influence estimation yields a favorable accuracy--memory trade-off for scalable long-context inference.

Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range under fixed budgets. articles.content:

Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. We introduce a loop-recovery mechanism to filter candidates away from repeated behaviors and a conservative, unanimous DONE gating policy that requires absolute consensus to terminate. Abstract: Populations vary along cultural dimensions such as individualism, collectivism, and honor. We evaluate our models through multiple methods: document retrieval, semantic textual similarity, questionnaire-item classification, and validation against expert annotations. Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25071v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. articles.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25191v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers about capitals of former states teaches the model to refuse 98% of such capitals on new questions, a loss that accuracy and abstention rates do not reveal. Abstract: Post-hoc rewriting is used to reduce demographic disparities in LLM-generated text when the source model is inaccessible. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25289v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). Abstract: Browsers now ship local language models to ordinary endpoints. Google includes Gemini Nano in Chrome to enable productivity features such as summarization, with inference running entirely on the device. These browser-embedded models provide new living-off-the-land opportunities for attackers, each instance a potential post-exploitation engine already installed, signed by the vendor, and invisible to network monitoring. The Gemini model is multimodal, capable of processing files, analyzing screenshots, or conversing with an attacker. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) applied singly and in combination against a matched control, and a seven-signal scoring rubric. articles.content:

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can only teach a language model what its reward can recognize. Answer checkers are exact but need a reference answer; learned reward models and LLM judges work everywhere, but their scores are not probabilities. We study RLCDR (Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards). An LLM converted into a decision model answers a typed question about a response ("is the final answer correct?", "which step is the first error?") with a probability distribution, read in one forward pass, debiased over option orders and calibrated with about a hundred labels. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. Abstract: Localizing object boundaries is important for embodied visual systems, since small boundary errors can change the inferred geometry of physical surfaces. We study whether deep stereo models produce boundaries consistent with simple shape priors when local image and disparity cues are weak. We create a synthetic stereo dataset consisting of objects drawn from a highly constrained family of shapes, with randomized depth, slant, color and texture. Despite the simplicity of this shape space, we find that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors, even when finetuned or trained from scratch on the dataset. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cross-modal knowledge distillation can incur negative transfer when source-modality supervision conflicts with the target modality's discriminative characteristics. We propose TALD, a two-stage framework for Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement in class-aligned logit space. Guided by task-dependent self-benefiting and cross-modal exclusivity criteria, a Residual Disentangler decomposes logits from a teacher and an independently trained target-modality reference student into modality-general and modality-specific components. A Sample-Adaptive Modulator regulates decomposition constraints and sample-specific fusion weights. The learned modality-general components are then adaptively fused to supervise the final student. Across five benchmarks spanning vision, audio, and text, TALD achieves the largest mean accuracy gain and highest positive-transfer frequency among the compared methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A calibrated decision model can predict how often each answer is chosen. The same prediction can reflect disagreement among people who are confident in their choices or uncertainty among people who share a belief. Disagreement calls for identifying whose perspective applies, while uncertainty calls for gathering more evidence. Standard post-training scores a single prediction against one observed choice at a time, learning the pooled distribution without distinguishing these two sources of uncertainty. We introduce Belief-Grouped Policy Optimization (BGPO). The policy proposes a list of beliefs, estimates their prevalence, and predicts a choice distribution for each. During training, BGPO uses Bayes' rule to estimate how likely each belief was to generate an observed choice. These estimates weight the choice's contribution to each belief's log-score reward. Abstract: JEPA-based video encoders learn strong representations for video and image understanding through prediction in latent space. articles.content:

Abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Whole-body human recognition has advanced rapidly with large vision models. However, existing methods remain fragile under real-world variations, as they tie identity to transient cues such as clothing, texture, pose, or viewpoint. We argue that a robust recognizer should not merely learn to ignore these cues, but imagine how a person would be represented if they changed. To this end, we propose IDWorld, an identity world model: just as a latent world model predicts the features of a scene after an action, IDWorld predicts how a person would be represented under a changed condition. In a single forward pass, IDWorld imagines these counterfactual features under shared canonical conditions, such as the same outfit, a fixed view, or a bare silhouette, without rendering any pixels. articles.title: Recurrent Vision Language Models Solve the Shell Game
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tracking a hidden object through a video is effortless for humans, yet it remains a bottleneck for vision language models (VLMs). In the shell game, where a ball is hidden under one of several identical cups that are then swapped, VLMs that answer directly stay near chance, thinking models fail on long games, and fine-tuning learns only the lengths it has seen. We argue that the limit is serial computation: each swap must be composed with the last result, and a VLM of fixed depth has only a fixed number of state transitions for it. To address this, we propose RecurrentVLM, which makes every attention layer of a pretrained VLM recur over time by computing the keys and values of finished frame groups from the layer's own output. Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Abstract: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. We present Accord, which constructs an accurate online dense metric map from any camera with an IMU. articles.title: CalibCache: Cache-to-Full Feature Dynamics Calibration for Diffusion Transformers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion Transformers generate high-quality images, but iterative sampling remains computationally expensive. Feature caching reduces the number of full network evaluations, yet its approximation error can become more severe under short sampling schedules, where fewer full-compute steps and a coarser sampling grid can make history-based extrapolation less reliable. In this paper, we propose CalibCache, a lightweight offline calibration method that corrects systematic discrepancies between cached and full-compute feature dynamics. Specifically, CalibCache calibrates feature acceleration, defined as the second-order finite difference across sampling steps. Using only a single pair of full-compute and naive-cache trajectories at each setting, CalibCache fits scalar acceleration maps offline by centered least squares. These maps are then applied during sampling without additional full-network evaluations or online optimization. Across FLUX.

Abstract: GUI grounding maps a screenshot and a natural language instruction to the coordinates of the intended interface element. Existing approaches improve grounding through visual scaling, instruction scaling, and sampling scaling, yet it remains unclear which grounding bottlenecks these strategies address and where their gains saturate. To address this gap, we introduce ScaleDiag, a controlled diagnostic framework that isolates the effects of visual input, instruction information, and prediction sampling on GUI grounding by independently varying target scale and surrounding context, target-specific information and auxiliary descriptions, and candidate coverage and selection, respectively. We evaluate ScaleDiag across five benchmarks and up to eight vision-language models and find that each scaling strategy operates within a much narrower regime than commonly assumed. Abstract: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25067v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. articles.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. Abstract: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation. Existing methods address these limitations by introducing intermediate subgoals, either generated by learned models or selected from experience memory. articles.title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25138v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. On nuScenes and nuPlan, the best textbook planners are competitive (L2 error of 0.735\,m against 0.947\,m for UniAD's planner; a nuPlan score of 79.3 against 76.1 for the rule-based PDM-Closed on Test14-hard with reactive agents). articles.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.

Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). articles.content:

Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. Abstract: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. Abstract: Learning-based planners are sensitive to the long-tailed distribution of driving data. Common maneuvers dominate datasets, while dangerous or rare scenarios are sparse. This imbalance can bias models toward the frequent cases and degrade performance on critical scenarios. To tackle this problem, we compare balancing strategies for sampling training data and find reweighting by trajectory pattern an effective approach. We further introduce moderated, in-the-loop guidance that injects small perturbation between flow steps to systematically increase trajectory diversity while remaining scene-consistent. Abstract: We propose LCLA (Language-Conditioned Latent Alignment), a framework for vision-language navigation that learns modular perception-action interfaces by aligning sensory observations to a latent representation of an expert policy. The expert is first trained with privileged state information, inducing a latent space sufficient for control, after which its latent interface and action head are frozen. A lightweight adapter is then trained to map raw visual-language observations, via a frozen vision-language model, into the expert's latent space, reducing the problem of visuomotor learning to supervised latent alignment rather than end-to-end policy optimization. This decoupling enforces a stable contract between perception and control, enabling expert behavior to be reused across sensing modalities and environmental variations. Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often bundle architectural changes with different pretraining data, backbone scales, and optimization recipes, obscuring what actually drives progress. We introduce SimVLA, a deliberately minimal VLA, a standard vision-language backbone with a lightweight continuous-action head, as a controlled testbed for this attribution problem; our contribution is methodological and empirical (a controlled attribution study and a minimal-baseline calibration), not a new technique. articles.content: Scaling Law在空间智能这里失效了？    作者丨周蕾    编辑丨岑峰                                                                                                       今年初字节的Seedance 2.0发布时，“电影级别”的出片质量让不少从业者倍感兴奋和震撼，新的创作蓝图正在他们面前徐徐展开——但对商汤的Seko团队来说，那是一段“迷茫”的日子。商汤联合创始人、首席科学家林达华在最近一次访谈中回忆，那段时间他去见投资人、参加行业会议，被问到的几乎总是同一个问题：你们的Seko和Seedance有什么区别？做得过它吗？团队里一度出现自我怀疑的声音：这件事还要不要做下去？后来故事并没有走向商汤Seko单枪匹马“对抗”Seedance的结局。Seedance把30秒的视频片段渲染到顶级水准；而Seko面向的创作者，最终交付的是100集的短剧——这中间隔着剧本、分镜、人物设定和跨剧集的形象一致性，是一整套创作流程。想清楚了这件事，Seko反而活得更好了：据林达华在访谈中透露，今年这款产品的用户增长了7到8倍，平台上产出了播放量过亿的短剧。对于商汤在大模型市场上的声量，林达华自己有个坦率的评价：“可能不是最大的”。这家公司的路线，也始终没有完全跟着行业最热的方向走。但商汤有一个坚持多年的习惯：直到今天，公司依然有20%的资源，投入给没有任何产品出口的预研工作。某种程度来说，这也是一种“播种”，种子下地时其实无需承诺收成。汤晓鸥常挂在嘴边的那句话——life finds a way，“生命自寻出路”，或许正是这笔投入的逻辑。在最近参加的微博科技 X 卫诗婕联合出品的《科技漫谈》栏目访谈中，林达华从行业的现状聊起，穿过商业化的验证，最后落在智能的边界上。但贯穿始终的线索只有一个：那20%的资源，以及支撑它的判断——为什么有的路值得走得很长、很久，哪怕眼下仍未看见出口。01训练成本停不下来，拼手速的中国AI大模型行业的钱，正在以一种停不下来的方式烧下去。行业里曾经有一个普遍假设：花巨大代价训出一个好模型，成本就能摊薄到之后的规模化服务里。林达华在访谈中指出，这个假设未必成立——问题不在模型不够好，而是“你不继续训下一个，别人就会超过你”。竞争逼着公司一轮接一轮地重训，训练成本因此停不下来，而且越滚越大。尽管过去一年的行业叙事，几乎被“更大即更强”占据，但卷参数这条路正在遭到反噬。他提到两个信号：一是模型的体量选择变得更务实。最近各家厂商均发布了Flash级别的中小模型：GLM 5.3 Flash、DeepSeek 4.1 Flash，谷歌和OpenAI也推出了同类规格的产品。林达华在访谈中特别提到了DeepSeek的表现：“4.1的Flash，它的性能水平是比4.0 Pro是要好的。”一个几百B量级、训练调优精良的模型跑赢上一代Pro，说明中等体量上的优化空间还远没有吃完。二是预训练数据的质量被重新摆上桌面。当几千亿参数的模型在实战中跑赢了2万亿参数的对手，很多人开始回头检查自己的数据管线。林达华对此有一个形象的解释：“（数据里）有很多的杂质、很多的东西相互打架，使得中间的很多的效率就会被抵扣掉。”结果就是一个又贵又不理想的模型，参数堆上去了，效果没上去。“当所有人很盲目地去做参数量的竞争，我觉得并不是一种健康的状态。”在他看来，这两个信号意味着行业正在回归理性：不再围着单一指标较劲，而是回到最终用户的价值上。上一轮AI周期里，类似情况也出现过，商汤自己就是亲历者。每个项目都要从收集数据开始，专门训练、调优、测试，全流程重做一遍，很难真正复制。只是当年的计量单位是项目，今天换成了参数。拼手速是另一种内卷的形态。美国的前沿实验室定义着SOTA的天花板，新模型一发布，等于给中国的从业者们指了一条路——国内往往在两三个月内涌出一批宣称采用同类方案的产品，抢占生态位，最近大热的RSI（递归自我改进）同样是一堆公司在同时开建。“说实话，拼手速这个事其实是蛮累的。”林达华观察

This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

articles.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

articles.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
articles.content: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

articles.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
articles.content: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

articles.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
articles.content: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.
